Who was the first Hyderabad Muslim leader to join the Indian National Congress?
x:
Mulla Abdul Qayyum was the first prominent Muslim leader from Hyderabad State to join the Indian National Congress. He actively supported educational reforms, political awakening and constitutional reforms in Hyderabad. He is regarded as one of the pioneers of modern political consciousness among Muslims in the Hyderabad State.

Option (3).

s: Wahabi Movement was:
x:
The Wahabi Movement was an Islamic revivalist movement that gradually assumed an anti-British character in India. Many Wahabi leaders opposed British rule and attempted to organize resistance against colonial authority during the nineteenth century. Consequently, the British considered the movement a political threat and took severe action against its leaders.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (1).

s: Who was the leader of the Wahabi movement, an anti-British movement by Andhra Muslims in the 19th century?
x:
Mubariz-ud-Daula, the brother of the Nizam of Hyderabad, became the chief supporter of the Wahabi Movement in Hyderabad State. Influenced by Syed Ahmed Barelvi, he attempted to organize resistance against growing British influence in the Deccan. His activities alarmed both the British and the Nizam's administration. Under British pressure, he was arrested and imprisoned, where he remained until his death.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (3).
